title: Daily foundation
tagline: A few simple, proven basics for most healthy adults.
for: Healthy adults who want a simple, evidence-first daily routine.

items.title: Get outdoor daylight
items.notes: Daylight is the best source of bright light by day. It helps your body clock and sleep.

items.title: Brisk walk
items.notes: Aim for 150 minutes a week that makes you a bit out of breath. Any amount is better than none.

items.title: Strength session
items.notes: Work all major muscles at least 2 days a week. Body weight or bands are fine. Skip a day if sore.

items.title: Vitamin D3 10 µg (400 IU)
items.notes: Take if you get little sun on your skin: autumn and winter, or all year if you are rarely outdoors or have dark skin.

items.title: Omega-3 250 mg (fish or algae oil)
items.notes: Only if you eat less than 1 portion of oily fish a week. Food first: 1 portion (140 g) of oily fish a week.

items.title: Protein at every meal
items.notes: Aim for about 0.8 g of protein per kg body weight a day, spread over your meals.

items.title: Fibre: aim for 30 g a day
items.notes: Vegetables, fruit, beans, whole grains, nuts and seeds. Build up slowly over a few weeks.

items.title: Wind down for sleep
items.notes: Screens off 30 minutes before bed. Aim for 7 or more hours, at the same times each day.

safety: Vitamin D: do not take more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day in total from all supplements.
Check other products (like multivitamins) so you don't double up on vitamin D.
Kidney disease or high calcium: ask your doctor before taking vitamin D.
On blood thinners? Tell your doctor before starting fish oil.
Heart rhythm problems such as atrial fibrillation? Ask your doctor first. Omega-3 supplements slightly raised this risk in trials, more so above 1 g a day.
Pregnant, planning a pregnancy or breastfeeding? Ask your midwife or doctor for the right plan.
New to exercise? Start small and build up slowly.

keyStudies.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
keyStudies.finding: Adults should do 150-300 minutes of moderate activity a week plus strength work on 2 or more days.

keyStudies.title: Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts
keyStudies.finding: More daily steps were linked to lower risk of death, levelling off at 6,000-8,000 (age 60+) and 8,000-10,000 (under 60).

keyStudies.title: Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
keyStudies.finding: Eating 25-29 g of fibre a day was linked to the biggest drop in disease risk. Trials showed lower weight, blood pressure and cholesterol.

keyStudies.title: Vitamin D for the Prevention of Disease: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
keyStudies.finding: Advises against vitamin D above daily needs for healthy adults under 75, and against routine testing.

keyStudies.title: Omega-3 fatty acids for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease
keyStudies.finding: Omega-3 supplements had little or no effect on deaths, with a small drop in heart disease events (low certainty).

keyStudies.title: Effect of Long-Term Marine Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation on the Risk of Atrial Fibrillation
keyStudies.finding: Omega-3 supplements were linked to more atrial fibrillation, especially at doses above 1 g a day.

title: Desk worker day
tagline: Short, regular movement breaks for long days at a desk.
for: Office and remote staff who sit for long periods at work.
notFor: anyone told by a doctor to limit their activity

items.title: Morning daylight
items.notes: Step outside soon after waking. Daylight is the best source of bright light for your body clock.

items.title: Sitting break: walk 2-3 minutes
items.notes: Every 20-30 minutes of sitting, get up and walk for 2-3 minutes. A timer helps.

items.title: Walk after meals
items.notes: A 10-minute walk soon after eating helps keep blood sugar steadier after meals.

items.title: Stand for calls
items.notes: Stand for phone or video calls. If you have a sit-stand desk, switch position through the day.

items.title: Drink water through the day
items.notes: Aim for 6-8 glasses of fluid a day. Water, tea and coffee all count. Drink more in hot weather.

items.title: Rest your eyes
items.notes: Every 20-30 minutes, look at something far away for a few seconds. Studies are small and mixed.

items.title: Vitamin D3 10 µg (400 IU)
items.notes: Only if you get little sun on your skin, for example if you work indoors and are rarely outside.

items.title: Weekly activity target
items.notes: Breaks and walks all count. Aim for 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, plus strength work twice a week.

safety: Stop and get medical advice if walking brings on chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
On insulin or tablets like gliclazide or glimepiride? Walking can lower blood sugar. Know the signs of a low.
Vitamin D: no more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day in total from all supplements.
Kidney disease or high calcium: ask your doctor before taking vitamin D.
Eye strain, headaches or blurry vision that keep coming back: get your eyes checked.

keyStudies.title: Breaking up prolonged sitting reduces postprandial glucose and insulin responses
keyStudies.finding: 2-minute walks every 20 minutes lowered blood sugar and insulin after a drink compared with sitting still.

keyStudies.title: The Acute Effects of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting Time in Adults with Standing and Light-Intensity Walking on Biomarkers of Cardiometabolic Health in Adults
keyStudies.finding: Light walking breaks lowered blood sugar and insulin after meals. Standing breaks helped less.

keyStudies.title: Advice to walk after meals is more effective for lowering postprandial glycaemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus than advice that does not specify timing
keyStudies.finding: 10-minute walks after each meal lowered post-meal blood sugar more than one 30-minute walk a day.

keyStudies.title: Effectiveness of an intervention for reducing sitting time and improving health in office workers: three arm cluster randomised controlled trial
keyStudies.finding: A workplace programme plus a sit-stand desk cut sitting by about an hour a day after 12 months.

keyStudies.title: The impact of break schedules on digital eye strain symptoms and ocular accommodation during prolonged near work
keyStudies.finding: Regular or self-paced breaks eased eye strain compared with no breaks in a 40-minute reading task.

title: Iron top-up (low iron confirmed)
tagline: Every-other-day iron, timed well, with planned blood tests.
for: Adults whose blood test shows low iron (low ferritin) and whose doctor has advised iron tablets.
notFor: no blood test showing low iron

items.title: Iron 65 mg (one ferrous sulfate 200 mg tablet)
items.notes: Doctor-supervised dose for a confirmed deficiency, above the daily limit for healthy people. Every other morning on an empty stomach. Follow your doctor's dose.

items.title: 2-hour gap: tea, coffee, dairy, eggs
items.notes: On iron days, keep tea, coffee, milk, eggs and calcium 2 hours away from your iron tablet.

items.title: Vitamin C is optional
items.notes: A large trial found adding vitamin C did not help iron work better. A glass of orange juice is fine if your doctor suggests it.

items.title: Iron-rich foods
items.notes: Meat, fish, beans, lentils, tofu and fortified cereals. Eat fruit or vegetables with plant sources to help absorption.

items.title: Side effects check-in
items.notes: Tell your doctor about stomach pain, sickness or constipation. Every-other-day dosing may be easier on the stomach.

items.title: Blood test: is the iron working?
items.notes: Your doctor checks haemoglobin within about 4 weeks of starting.

items.title: Blood test: ferritin and blood count
items.notes: Iron is usually continued for about 3 months after haemoglobin is normal, to refill stores. Your doctor decides whether to continue and for how long.

safety: Only take iron if a blood test shows low iron and your doctor agrees.
This dose is above the daily upper limit for healthy people (40-45 mg). Use it only for a confirmed deficiency, under a doctor's care.
Never take iron if you have haemochromatosis (iron overload).
Keep iron tablets out of reach of children. An iron overdose can kill a young child.
Take thyroid tablets (levothyroxine) at least 4 hours apart from iron.
Indigestion medicines can lower iron absorption. Ask your pharmacist about timing.
Low iron needs a cause found, especially in men and in women after menopause. Your doctor will advise on checks.
Pregnant? Your midwife or doctor will set your iron plan.
After the course, ask your doctor about a repeat blood count (often about 6 months later) to catch low iron coming back.

keyStudies.title: Iron absorption from oral iron supplements given on consecutive versus alternate days and as single morning doses versus twice-daily split dosing in iron-depleted women: two open-label, randomised controlled trials
keyStudies.finding: In women with low iron, 60 mg every other day was absorbed better than daily. Splitting into two doses a day did not help.

keyStudies.title: Iron absorption from supplements is greater with alternate day than with consecutive day dosing in iron-deficient anemic women
keyStudies.finding: Small isotope crossover study in 19 women (only dose order randomised): absorption was 40-50% higher on an alternate day than on the second day in a row.

keyStudies.title: Alternate day versus daily oral iron for treatment of iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial
keyStudies.finding: In 200 adults, alternate-day and daily iron raised haemoglobin by a similar amount over 8 weeks.

keyStudies.title: Efficacy of daily versus alternate day oral iron supplementation for management of anaemia among general population: a systematic review and meta-analysis
keyStudies.finding: 11 trials: daily and alternate-day iron worked about the same. Alternate-day was better tolerated. Very low certainty.

keyStudies.title: The Efficacy and Safety of Vitamin C for Iron Supplementation in Adult Patients With Iron Deficiency Anemia: A Randomized Clinical Trial
keyStudies.finding: In 440 adults, adding vitamin C to iron did not improve haemoglobin or ferritin.

keyStudies.title: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults
keyStudies.finding: One iron tablet a day, or every other day if side effects. Check response within 4 weeks. Continue about 3 months after haemoglobin is normal.

title: Blood sugar support
tagline: Daily habits that help keep blood sugar steadier, alongside your care.
for: Adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, working with their doctor or diabetes team.
notFor: trouble swallowing or a narrowed bowel (for psyllium)

items.title: Walk after meals
items.notes: A 10-minute walk soon after each main meal lowers the rise in blood sugar after eating.

items.title: Movement break from sitting
items.notes: Every 20-30 minutes of sitting, get up and walk for 2-3 minutes.

items.title: Strength session
items.notes: Strength work on at least 2 days a week, plus 150 minutes of moderate activity a week.

items.title: Vegetables and protein first, carbs last
items.notes: Eat the vegetables and protein on your plate before the bread, rice, pasta or potatoes. Use this at lunch and dinner.

items.title: Psyllium husk 5 g before breakfast
items.notes: Stir into a large glass of water (at least 150 ml) and drink straight away. Ask your pharmacist how to time it with your medicines.

items.title: Psyllium husk 5 g before dinner
items.notes: Stir into a large glass of water (at least 150 ml). Not right before bed. Start with one dose a day for the first week if you feel bloated.

items.title: Sleep 7-8 hours
items.notes: The lowest diabetes risk is seen with 7-8 hours of sleep. Keep regular sleep times.

items.title: B12 blood test if you take metformin
items.notes: Long-term metformin can lower vitamin B12. Ask your doctor about a test, and repeat checks if you have risk factors.

items.title: Vitamin D and magnesium: ask first
items.notes: Vitamin D trials in prediabetes found a small drop in diabetes risk. Ask your doctor before taking it. Take magnesium only if a test shows it is low.

safety: Keep taking your diabetes medicines. This routine adds to your care. It does not replace it.
Psyllium and these habits can lower blood sugar. Tell your doctor before starting, as your medicines may need adjusting.
On insulin, gliclazide or glimepiride? Know the signs of a low (shaky, sweaty, hungry, confused) and carry a sugary drink on walks.
Always take psyllium with plenty of water. Do not take it if you have trouble swallowing, a narrowed bowel or a sudden change in bowel habit.
Keep psyllium 30-60 minutes apart from other medicines, as it can slow their absorption. Ask your pharmacist about timing.
Berberine and chromium are doctor-only. They can push blood sugar too low with diabetes medicines.
Stop exercise and get help if you have chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness.
Vitamin D: no more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day in total unless your doctor advises it.

keyStudies.title: Advice to walk after meals is more effective for lowering postprandial glycaemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus than advice that does not specify timing
keyStudies.finding: In 41 adults with type 2 diabetes, 10-minute walks after meals lowered post-meal blood sugar more than one daily walk.

keyStudies.title: Nutrient intake order on metabolic outcomes in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
keyStudies.finding: Eating carbs last lowered blood sugar 1 hour after meals and HbA1c a little (0.16%).

keyStudies.title: The impact of food order on postprandial glycaemic excursions in prediabetes
keyStudies.finding: In prediabetes, eating protein and vegetables before carbs cut the blood sugar peak by over 40%.

keyStudies.title: Psyllium fiber improves glycemic control proportional to loss of glycemic control: a meta-analysis
keyStudies.finding: Psyllium before meals lowered fasting glucose and HbA1c in type 2 diabetes, less in prediabetes, and not in people with normal blood sugar.

keyStudies.title: Long-term Metformin Use and Vitamin B12 Deficiency in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study
keyStudies.finding: Long-term metformin was linked to low B12. Authors advise considering routine B12 tests.

keyStudies.title: Vitamin D and Risk for Type 2 Diabetes in People With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Individual Participant Data From 3 Randomized Clinical Trials
keyStudies.finding: Vitamin D lowered the risk of developing diabetes by 15% in people with prediabetes.

keyStudies.title: Sleep duration and risk of type 2 diabetes: a meta-analysis of prospective studies
keyStudies.finding: Observational: the lowest diabetes risk was seen with 7-8 hours of sleep a night.

title: Vein health
tagline: Calf-pump moves, leg rest and stockings, with doctor-guided vein supplements.
for: Adults with varicose veins or chronic venous insufficiency, alongside their doctor's care.
notFor: a hot, red, swollen or painful leg (see a doctor today)
a leg ulcer or a bleeding vein
poor blood flow in the legs (for stockings)

items.title: Calf pumps: heel raises
items.notes: Rise onto your toes and lower slowly, 15-20 times. Hold a chair for balance. Repeat later in the day.

items.title: Daily walk
items.notes: Regular walking helps blood flow in the legs. Build up slowly.

items.title: Break from sitting or standing
items.notes: Avoid long spells of sitting or standing. Every 30 minutes, walk or do ankle pumps.

items.title: Legs up
items.notes: Lie down with your legs raised on cushions.

items.title: Put on compression stockings
items.notes: Only if a doctor or nurse has advised and fitted them. Stockings of at least 15 mmHg ease aching and swelling.

items.title: Diosmin + hesperidin (MPFF) 1000 mg
items.notes: Doctor-first. Micronised diosmin 900 mg + hesperidin 100 mg once a day. Allow at least 4 weeks to judge it.

items.title: Alternative: horse chestnut extract
items.notes: Only if your doctor prefers it to MPFF: standardised seed extract, 50 mg aescin twice a day. Never take both.

safety: Get medical help the same day for a hot, red, swollen or painful leg. It can be a blood clot (DVT).
Call emergency services if leg pain or swelling comes with breathlessness or chest pain.
If a varicose vein bleeds: lie down, raise the leg and press firmly on it. Then get urgent help.
See your GP for pain, itching or swelling, a sore that has not healed in 2 weeks, or veins that get worse.
Before stockings, have the blood flow in your legs checked, especially if you have diabetes or poor circulation.
Vein supplements may ease heaviness and swelling. They are not shown to make varicose veins go away.
Use only one vein supplement, chosen with your doctor. Stomach upset is the most common side effect.
Horse chestnut extract: older labels give 50 mg aescin a dose; newer EU labels give 21 mg as protoaescigenin. Ask your pharmacist.
Horse chestnut: only standardised seed extract. Raw seeds, bark, flowers and leaves are poisonous.
Horse chestnut is not advised in pregnancy, breastfeeding or under 18. With heart or kidney problems, ask your doctor.
On blood thinners or planning surgery? Ask your doctor first. Supplements are often stopped 2 weeks before surgery.

keyStudies.title: European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2022 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Chronic Venous Disease of the Lower Limbs
keyStudies.finding: Recommends stockings (at least 15 mmHg) for symptoms, suggests exercise, and says venoactive drugs should be considered for symptoms and swelling.

keyStudies.title: Phlebotonics for venous insufficiency
keyStudies.finding: Vein drugs probably reduce leg swelling slightly, with little effect on quality of life and slightly more side effects.

keyStudies.title: Efficacy of micronized purified flavonoid fraction on improving individual symptoms, signs and quality of life in patients with chronic venous disease
keyStudies.finding: 7 placebo-controlled trials (1,692 people): MPFF eased leg pain, heaviness, cramps and swelling.

keyStudies.title: The Effects of Different Dosages on Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction's Treatment of Lower Limb Chronic Venous Disease
keyStudies.finding: 1000 mg once a day worked as well as 500 mg twice a day.

keyStudies.title: Horse chestnut seed extract for chronic venous insufficiency
keyStudies.finding: Horse chestnut extract eased leg pain and swelling short term. Larger trials are still needed.

keyStudies.title: Physical exercise for the treatment of non-ulcerated chronic venous insufficiency
keyStudies.finding: 5 small trials (146 people). Exercise may help calf pump and venous refilling, but certainty is very low.

title: Surgery prep and recovery
tagline: Simple steps before and after a planned operation, led by your surgical team.
for: Adults with a planned (non-emergency) operation. Day 0 is the day of surgery: negative days are before, positive days after.
notFor: a special diet or exercise plan set by your surgical team

items.title: Before: list every supplement for your team
items.notes: Write down every vitamin, herbal remedy and supplement, with doses. Bring the bottles to your pre-op visit.

items.title: Before: pause supplements if told to
items.notes: Your team may ask you to stop supplements at least 2 weeks before surgery. Follow their plan.

items.title: Before: daily walk
items.notes: Stay active until surgery if your team agrees. Prehab programmes shortened hospital stays in trials.

items.title: Before: smoke-free day (if you smoke)
items.notes: Stopping smoking before surgery lowers the risk of problems afterwards. Ask your GP or pharmacist for support.

items.title: Before: alcohol-free day (if you drink a lot)
items.notes: More than 3 drinks a day? Get your doctor's help to stop. You may need medicine for withdrawal.

items.title: After: short walks as allowed
items.notes: Get up and walk as soon as your team says it is safe. Add a little more each day.

items.title: After: breathing exercises from your team
items.notes: If you are shown breathing or physio exercises, do them as taught. They can cut chest problems after tummy surgery.

items.title: After: protein at every meal
items.notes: Eat as soon as your team allows. Aim for about 1.2-1.5 g protein per kg body weight a day unless told otherwise. Kidney disease: ask first.

items.title: After: restart supplements only with an OK
items.notes: Ask before restarting supplements. Don't add new 'healing' mixes: most have no proof of benefit.

safety: Your surgical team's advice comes first. This plan does not replace it.
Never stop prescribed medicines, including blood thinners, unless your team tells you to.
Often paused 1-2 weeks before surgery: ginkgo, garlic, ginseng, ginger, high-dose turmeric, feverfew, saw palmetto, horse chestnut, high-dose vitamin E.
Kava, valerian and St John's wort can affect anaesthesia. Tell your anaesthetist.
Fish oil: a large heart-surgery trial found no extra bleeding. Ask your team whether to continue.
Heavy drinker? Don't stop suddenly on your own. Ask your doctor for help.
After surgery, get urgent help for a hot, red, swollen or painful leg, chest pain or sudden breathlessness.
Kidney disease: ask before raising your protein.
Follow your team's advice on wound care, lifting and driving.

keyStudies.title: Preoperative Management of Surgical Patients Using Dietary Supplements: SPAQI Consensus Statement
keyStudies.finding: Ask every patient about supplements. Without proven benefit, there is little downside to pausing them before surgery.

keyStudies.title: ESPEN guideline on clinical nutrition in surgery - Update 2025
keyStudies.finding: Avoid long fasting, eat again early after surgery, and get moving early to help protein use and muscle.

keyStudies.title: Effects of Nutritional Prehabilitation, With and Without Exercise, on Outcomes of Patients Who Undergo Colorectal Surgery
keyStudies.finding: Prehab before bowel surgery cut hospital stay by about 2 days.

keyStudies.title: Preoperative smoking cessation interventions and their effects on smoking abstinence and postoperative outcomes
keyStudies.finding: Help to stop smoking before surgery probably cut complications by about 27%.

keyStudies.title: Perioperative alcohol cessation intervention for postoperative complications
keyStudies.finding: Intensive help to stop drinking 4-8 weeks before surgery probably reduced complications (3 small trials).

keyStudies.title: Fish Oil and Perioperative Bleeding
keyStudies.finding: In 1,516 heart-surgery patients, fish oil did not increase bleeding and fewer transfusions were needed.

keyStudies.title: Non-drug perioperative interventions to reduce postoperative pulmonary complications after abdominal surgery
keyStudies.finding: 255 trials: physiotherapy and early mobilisation were among measures that helped prevent chest complications.

title: Gut and microbiome
tagline: More fibre, fermented foods and plant variety, built up slowly.
for: Adults who want to support gut health through food and daily habits.
notFor: new or unexplained bowel symptoms (see your GP first)
a narrowed bowel or past bowel blockage

items.title: Add one fibre food
items.notes: Oats, beans, lentils, vegetables, fruit, nuts or seeds. Build up over about 4 weeks towards 30 g a day.

items.title: One fermented food
items.notes: Yogurt, kefir, kimchi, sauerkraut or kombucha. Start with 1 serving and add more slowly if you feel well.

items.title: Count your plants this week
items.notes: Aim for variety: vegetables, fruit, beans, grains, nuts, seeds and herbs. Linked to a more varied gut in a large survey, not a trial.

items.title: Drink water through the day
items.notes: Aim for 6-8 glasses of fluid a day. Water, tea and coffee all count.

items.title: Probiotic during antibiotics only
items.notes: Only while on antibiotics. Start within 2 days of the first dose. Take at a different time from the antibiotic (a practical tip, not tested).

items.title: Wind or bloating? Go slower
items.notes: Some wind or bloating is common when you add fermented foods or fibre. In a trial it settled with time.

items.title: What the app can and can't see
items.notes: Ticks track what you eat and do. The app cannot measure your gut bacteria, and people respond differently.

safety: See your GP if you notice blood in your poo, a lasting change in bowel habit, tummy pain, a lump, or weight loss without trying.
Get urgent advice for bloody diarrhoea, diarrhoea lasting more than 7 days, or signs of dehydration.
Do not take probiotics if your immune system is weak or you are seriously ill, unless your doctor says so.
Probiotic effects depend on the exact strain. Choose one tested in trials, such as S. boulardii or L. rhamnosus GG.
Experts disagree: one US guideline supports some probiotics with antibiotics, another advises against them.
IBS, IBD or coeliac disease? Ask your doctor or dietitian before big changes to fibre or fermented foods.
If more fibre causes pain, not just mild wind, slow down and get advice.

keyStudies.title: Gut-microbiota-targeted diets modulate human immune status
keyStudies.finding: In 36 adults over 17 weeks, more fermented foods raised gut microbe variety and lowered inflammation markers. High fibre did not raise variety in that time.

keyStudies.title: Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
keyStudies.finding: Fibre intakes of 25-29 g a day were linked to lower risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes and bowel cancer.

keyStudies.title: Probiotics for the prevention of Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea in adults and children
keyStudies.finding: During antibiotics, probiotics may cut C. difficile diarrhoea by half and antibiotic-linked diarrhoea by a third. Low certainty.

keyStudies.title: Probiotics for the Prevention of Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea in Outpatients-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
keyStudies.finding: 17 trials: diarrhoea in 8.0% with probiotics vs 17.7% without. No more side effects.

keyStudies.title: AGA Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Role of Probiotics in the Management of Gastrointestinal Disorders
keyStudies.finding: Suggests specific strains to prevent C. difficile in people on antibiotics. Probiotics for IBS and IBD only within trials.

title: Fascia and tissue support
tagline: Load your tissues well, eat enough protein, and time collagen before sessions.
for: Active adults doing regular strength or movement sessions who want to support tendons and connective tissue.
notFor: a new, hot, swollen or worsening injury (get it checked first)

items.title: Collagen 15 g + vitamin C 50 mg
items.notes: About 1 hour before your session, on training days. Trials used 15-30 g with about 50 mg vitamin C. Tendon results are mixed.

items.title: Strength or loading session
items.notes: Slow, controlled work for all major muscles, at least 2 days a week. Add load gradually.

items.title: Protein through the day
items.notes: If you train, aim for about 1.2-1.6 g protein per kg body weight a day, over 3-4 meals. More gave no extra gain.

items.title: Vitamin C foods
items.notes: Citrus, berries, kiwi, peppers or broccoli each day. Your body needs vitamin C to make collagen.

items.title: Vitamin D3 10 µg (400 IU)
items.notes: Only if you get little sun on your skin, for example in winter or if you are mostly indoors.

items.title: Mobility or foam rolling
items.notes: Gentle mobility or foam rolling improves range of motion for a short time, about as much as stretching.

safety: Kidney disease? Ask your doctor before raising protein or taking collagen.
Had kidney stones? Ask first. Gelatin raised urine oxalate in a study, and high-dose vitamin C can too.
Collagen is not a complete protein. It does not replace protein from meals.
Collagen and gelatin come from animals. Check the label if you avoid some animal foods.
Sharp pain, swelling, or pain that gets worse with loading: stop and see a physio or doctor.
Vitamin C: stay well below 2,000 mg a day.
Vitamin D: no more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day in total from all supplements.

keyStudies.title: Vitamin C-enriched gelatin supplementation before intermittent activity augments collagen synthesis
keyStudies.finding: In 8 men, 15 g gelatin with vitamin C 1 hour before exercise doubled a blood marker of collagen building.

keyStudies.title: The Collagen Synthesis Response to an Acute Bout of Resistance Exercise Is Greater when Ingesting 30 g Hydrolyzed Collagen Compared with 15 g and 0 g
keyStudies.finding: In 10 trained men, 30 g collagen with 50 mg vitamin C before squats raised collagen building more than 15 g or none.

keyStudies.title: The Effect of Specific Bioactive Collagen Peptides on Tendon Remodeling during 15 wk of Lower Body Resistance Training
keyStudies.finding: In 39 young men, 15 g collagen a day did not improve tendon changes from training more than placebo.

keyStudies.title: Hydrolysed Collagen Supplementation Enhances Patellar Tendon Adaptations to 12 Weeks' Resistance Training in Middle-Aged Men
keyStudies.finding: In 20 middle-aged men, 30 g collagen with vitamin C after training gave bigger gains in tendon size and stiffness.

keyStudies.title: Impact of Collagen Peptide Supplementation in Combination with Long-Term Physical Training: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
keyStudies.finding: 19 trials: collagen plus training gave small gains in lean mass, tendon size and strength. Low to very low certainty.

keyStudies.title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains
keyStudies.finding: 49 trials: extra protein boosted strength and muscle gains from training. No added gain above about 1.6 g/kg a day.

keyStudies.title: Acute Effects of Foam Rolling on Range of Motion in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review with Multilevel Meta-analysis
keyStudies.finding: 26 trials: foam rolling improved range of motion short term, about the same as stretching.

title: Plant-based essentials
tagline: The key nutrients to cover when you eat vegan or vegetarian.
for: Adults who eat a vegan or vegetarian diet.

items.title: Vitamin B12 10 µg
items.notes: Essential if you are vegan. At least 10 µg a day, or 2,000 µg once a week instead.

items.title: Iodine 150 µg
items.notes: Use a potassium iodide or iodate supplement, not kelp or seaweed. Skip if you have thyroid disease, unless your doctor agrees.

items.title: Algae omega-3 250 mg (EPA+DHA)
items.notes: Raises omega-3 levels in vegans. Not yet shown to prevent disease. Keep DHA under 1 g a day.

items.title: Vitamin D 10 µg (400 IU)
items.notes: Autumn and winter, or all year if you are rarely outdoors or have dark skin. Vegan D3 (from lichen) or D2.

items.title: 2-3 calcium-rich foods
items.notes: Calcium-set tofu, fortified plant milk or yogurt, kale, broccoli or tahini. If you can't, ask about a 500 mg supplement.

items.title: Iron and zinc foods at meals
items.notes: Beans, lentils, tofu, whole grains, nuts and seeds. Add vitamin C foods to meals. Keep tea and coffee between meals.

items.title: Blood test: B12, iron and vitamin D
items.notes: Ask your doctor about a check and how often to repeat it. For B12 in vegans, MMA or homocysteine tests are more reliable.

safety: Thyroid disease? Ask your doctor before taking iodine.
Don't use kelp or seaweed supplements for iodine. The amount varies a lot and can be far too high.
Iodine: stay under 600 µg a day in total.
Pregnant, planning a pregnancy or breastfeeding? Your needs change. Ask your midwife or doctor.
Only take iron or zinc supplements if a blood test or your doctor says you need them.
Vitamin D: no more than 100 µg (4,000 IU) a day in total.
Calcium supplements: 500 mg or less at a time. Had kidney stones? Ask first.
On blood thinners? Ask before taking omega-3.
A normal blood B12 result can be misleading in vegans. Keep taking B12 unless your doctor says otherwise.

keyStudies.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional vitamin B12 status among adult vegans
keyStudies.finding: Vegans had lower B12 and more signs of B12 shortage. Those taking B12 supplements had better results on every marker.

keyStudies.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of iodine nutrition in modern vegan and vegetarian diets
keyStudies.finding: Vegans had the lowest iodine intake and status, especially where salt is not iodised.

keyStudies.title: Vegan multinutrient supplementation significantly increases Omega-3 index and 25-OH-vitamin D status
keyStudies.finding: In 72 vegans, algae omega-3 plus vitamin D for 4 months raised omega-3 and vitamin D levels. A double dose added no clear benefit.

keyStudies.title: Scientific Opinion on the tolerable upper intake level for supplemental docosahexaenoic acid
keyStudies.finding: EFSA kept the safe level for DHA from supplements at 1 g a day for all adults.

keyStudies.title: Scientific Opinion on the Tolerable Upper Intake Level of EPA, DHA and DPA
keyStudies.finding: EFSA: EPA and DHA together up to about 5 g a day raise no safety concerns for adults.
